events.subtitle: 8th Anniversary Live / world-tour finale
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Toshiki Soejima's 8th Anniversary Live on January 5–6, 2027, with 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM starts each day. The seven-piece band closes a 13-city Europe, Asia and Oceania tour and adds guitarist Zack Auslander and saxophonist Hironori Ura to Soejima's Japanese ensemble. The venue lists a ¥7,000 music charge and published seat categories from ¥7,000 to ¥12,500 per person.

en.why_it_matters: Soejima's neo-soul guitar language is expanded here into a seven-piece band with a second guitar, trumpet, saxophone, keyboards and rhythm section, giving the tour finale more orchestral color than a routine club set. The point is the instrumental architecture and the way a Japanese online-guitar voice has grown into an international touring ensemble.
en.trip_verdict: Catch a set if early January already overlaps with Tokyo. Four performances make this easy to fit into a stay; it should enrich the itinerary rather than redirect it.

es.why_it_matters: El lenguaje de guitarra neo-soul de Soejima se amplía aquí a una banda de siete integrantes con segunda guitarra, trompeta, saxofón, teclados y sección rítmica, dando al cierre de gira más color orquestal que un set rutinario de club. Importan la arquitectura instrumental y el crecimiento de una voz japonesa nacida en línea hasta convertirse en ensamble internacional.
es.trip_verdict: Aprovecharía un set si Tokio ya coincide con principios de enero. Las cuatro funciones facilitan integrarlo a la estancia; debe enriquecer el itinerario, no desviarlo.

The venue bills this as Parlato's first collaboration with the 18-person orchestra and frames the repertoire around orchestral arrangements of her songs. The music charge is ¥10,500, with published seat categories from ¥10,500 to ¥16,000 per person.

Stage 1 admission rests on the first translation of Parlato's elastic vocal language into Miyashiro's 18-person brass-and-reeds setting. Stage 2 assigns A: the one-night arrangement question is worthwhile, but the recurring home orchestra and Parlato's following three-night run make A+ or scarcity language unnecessary.

en.why_it_matters: Parlato's voice usually works through breath, subdivision and close rhythmic conversation; placing it inside Miyashiro's 18-piece brass-and-reeds architecture creates a specific arranging problem worth hearing. The first collaboration asks how intimacy and negative space survive big-band scale.
en.trip_verdict: Attend conveniently if January 30 is open in Tokyo. If only one Parlato date fits, favor the following Wise Ones quartet for its current album repertoire and longer-form ensemble identity.

es.why_it_matters: La voz de Parlato suele trabajar con respiración, subdivisión y conversación rítmica cercana; ponerla dentro de la arquitectura de 18 metales y cañas de Miyashiro crea un problema de arreglo concreto que vale la pena escuchar. El primer encuentro pregunta cómo sobreviven la intimidad y el espacio negativo a escala de big band.
es.trip_verdict: Iría si el 30 de enero ya está libre en Tokio. Si sólo cabe una fecha de Parlato, elegiría el cuarteto The Wise Ones de los días siguientes por su repertorio actual y su identidad de ensamble de formato largo.

events.factual_description: National Sawdust presents The Seen and the Unseen on January 22, 2027 at 7:30 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM, as part of the PROTOTYPE Festival. The program pairs a 30-minute piano-only work-in-development presentation of Wang Lu and Deborah Brevoort's Red Thread, conducted by Anthony Cheung, with the approximately 45-minute fully staged world premiere of Daniel Zlatkin's HILMA, directed by Juliana Morales Carreño and performed by mezzo-soprano Catherine Martin with the National Sawdust Ensemble under Jeffrey Zeigler.

Stage 1 admission rests on the deliberate pairing of a Chinese-American adoption opera in development with the fully staged world premiere of HILMA. Stage 2 assigns A+: the premiere and multidisciplinary frame merit making room in a New York visit. S was rejected because the program is a festival development/premiere platform whose works are explicitly intended to have lives beyond this date; A+ captures the recommendation.

en.why_it_matters: The pairing exposes two different stages of opera becoming real: Red Thread strips a Chinese-American adoption story to piano, voice and myth while it is still being shaped; HILMA arrives fully staged, turning Hilma af Klint's unseen visions into light, movement and chamber sound. The contrast between workshop intimacy and world-premiere embodiment is the live argument.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room if New York is viable for PROTOTYPE. From the DMV, combine the Brooklyn night with another strong city reason rather than treating one festival program as a mandatory standalone trip.

es.why_it_matters: El programa deja visibles dos etapas distintas de cómo una ópera cobra forma: Red Thread reduce una historia de adopción chino-estadounidense a piano, voz y mito mientras todavía se construye; HILMA llega plenamente escenificada y convierte las visiones invisibles de Hilma af Klint en luz, movimiento y sonido de cámara. El contraste entre intimidad de laboratorio y encarnación de estreno mundial es el argumento en vivo.
es.trip_verdict: Le abriría espacio activamente si Nueva York resulta viable durante PROTOTYPE. Desde el DMV, combinaría la noche de Brooklyn con otra razón fuerte para estar en la ciudad en vez de tratar un solo programa de festival como viaje obligatorio.

Shawn Conley opens with Uncharted, interleaving Bach's first cello suite and free improvisation on solo double bass. Kinan Azmeh then leads a new acoustic trio with pianist Amino Belyamani and Conley, moving between composition and improvisation across multiple musical traditions.

La continuidad está en el bajo como puente, no como acompañamiento.
es.trip_verdict: Iría si una visita a Nueva York en febrero ya deja espacio para Williamsburg. El programa doble centrado en el instrumento recompensa el desvío, pero no justifica por sí solo un viaje por el corredor.
